normative_extracts.spec_section: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide — Roving tabindex
normative_extracts.quote: A composite widget places tabindex='0' on only its currently active descendant and tabindex='-1' on all other items, moving focus via Arrow keys so Tab exits the widget in one step.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: The browser's sequential focus navigation walks DOM order for tabindex='0' elements while skipping tabindex='-1' nodes, letting composite widgets own Arrow-key navigation.

production_failures.symptom: Keyboard users must press Tab 48 times to cross a toolbar or tablist
production_failures.root_cause: Every item inside a composite widget has tabindex='0' or native <button> without roving tabindex management.
production_failures.mitigation: Maintain tabindex='0' on only the active item and tabindex='-1' on siblings, moving focus with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight.

production_failures.symptom: Positive tabindex='5' breaks visual reading order across a refactored layout
production_failures.root_cause: Positive tabindex values override DOM order globally and drift out of sync whenever components reorder.
production_failures.mitigation: Ban positive tabindex (> 0) entirely; align DOM order with visual layout and use only 0 and -1.
